rows.notes: PE baseline rate mismatch: policyengine-us already has GA rate at 5.09% for 2026 (per prior HB1015 legislation), while the fiscal note treats the current rate as 5.19% (measuring from 2025 current-law baseline). The fiscal note measures the full 0.20pp cut (5.19%->4.99%), but PE natively only sees a 0.10pp cut (5.09%->4.99%) for year=2026.

provenance.source: Kansas Division of the Budget (KDOR estimate, Feb 20, 2026)

rows.notes: The fiscal note scores the same provisions PE modeled (standard deduction to $3,805/$8,640/$6,480 from TY2026, same baseline). Its fiscal-year mapping (FY2027 = 100% TY2026 + 30% TY2027) implies about -$10.6M for TY2026 vs PE's -$8.88M — a 16% smaller magnitude, plausibly because KDOR simulates actual Kansas returns (capturing all standard-deduction claimants) while PE uses survey-based microdata. The FY2026 column is zero and FY2027 stacks 130% of a tax year, so per-tax-year figures are the right comparison.

conditions.bill_title: CT SB78: SS Benefit Deduction Threshold Elimination

provenance.source: Connecticut OFA fiscal note for sSB-1 Sec. 6 (identical policy, enacted 5/26/26)

rows.notes: No OFA note exists for SB78 itself; the identical policy (full SS deduction for all filers) was enacted via SB 1 Sec. 6, which OFA scored at -$57.5M (General Fund, FY28, capturing tax year 2027 as enacted). PE's -$56.1M for TY2026 is within 2.4% - and a TY2026-basis OFA figure would be slightly smaller given benefit growth, tightening the agreement. Internally consistent with OFA's Tax Expenditure Report: the existing deduction costs $223M/yr, and extending only the remaining 25% exemption to above-threshold filers plausibly costs about a quarter of that.

conditions.bill_title: Utah HB210 S2: Marriage Penalty Removal

provenance.source: Utah Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst (2nd Sub. HB210, 2026-02-05)

rows.notes: The LFA scored exactly the version PE modeled (2nd Sub.), and the ongoing sign agrees: both score the bill as revenue-raising, because halving single/HOH phase-out thresholds outweighs the new ~$158 joint-filer credit. But magnitude diverges sharply: PE's +$11.48M is roughly 9x the LFA's steady-state +$1.29M/yr (Tax Commission data: ~113,000 taxpayers pay ~$161 more vs ~125,000 paying ~$150 less), suggesting PE over-scores the threshold-halving pickup or under-scores the credit. The note's FY2027 total nets to -$299,400 only because of a one-time -$1.59M item. The bill was later substituted through S05 and failed in the House 31-42.
